outcome: Nothing since 26 January 2024 settles, or moves a quantity named in, Jacobson's conjecture: the in-window items found (a May 2024 preprint on Jacobson radicals of Ore extensions and a March 2025 preprint on left Jacobson rings) are off-scope, and the conjecture is still described as open in general, with its positive cases all dating from 1974 to 2009.
problem_asks: Let R be a ring that is both left and right Noetherian, with Jacobson radical J = J(R). The bullet asks for (1) the intersection of the powers J^n over all n ≥ 1 to be exactly {0} (0 lies in every power, so the content is that no nonzero element does); (2) this for every such ring, with no further hypothesis (no commutativity, PI, fully bounded, finiteness or Krull-dimension restriction); (3) vanishing of that intersection, not nilpotence of J. Not asked by the bullet but part of its history: Jacobson's 1956 question was for one-sided (right) Noetherian rings and fails there by Herstein (1965); the two-sided hypothesis is what the bullet imposes.

events.what_happened: I. N. Herstein, 'A counterexample in Noetherian rings', Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. USA 54 (1965) 1036–1037, gives a ring built over Z(2) (rationals with denominator prime to 2) in which the powers of the Jacobson radical do not intersect to 0, answering Jacobson's 1956 question negatively for one-sided Noetherian rings. Known only from secondary descriptions (Wikipedia; a Kucera seminar abstract; the Brown–Lenagan note). The PNAS page refused the fetch.
events.delivers: A right Noetherian ring, not left Noetherian, with a nonzero intersection of powers of J, so the one-sided form of the question is false. Restriction: the ring is one-sided Noetherian.
events.remains: Nothing of the bullet, which requires left and right Noetherian, a hypothesis this ring does not satisfy.

checked_by.who: K. A. Brown and T. H. Lenagan
checked_by.qualification: ring theorists publishing in the Glasgow Mathematical Journal
checked_by.what_they_did: 1982 note explains why a ring similar in appearance to Herstein's example does satisfy the intersection property; the example's validity is not disputed in any source I read

events.direction: Cuts against the one-sided form of Jacobson's question (right Noetherian rings). It does not touch the two-sided statement in the bullet, since the ring is not left Noetherian.
events.object: A specific noncommutative ring over Z(2), right Noetherian but not left Noetherian, in which the intersection of the powers of J is nonzero. Explicit construction, not a non-constructive existence proof. I did not read the construction; the description rests on secondary sources.

events.what_happened: A. V. Jategaonkar, 'Left principal ideal domains' (1968), gives a further counterexample to the one-sided question. Wikipedia calls it a left principal ideal domain; a search-result summary describes a family of right principal ideal domains whose right ideals are exactly the powers of J. Not read in the original; the sidedness is disputed.
events.delivers: A one-sided counterexample to the statement that the intersection of the powers of J is zero. Whether it is two-sided Noetherian is not established by my sources.
events.remains: Whether it bears on the bullet at all depends on the open fact in delivers: if the example is two-sided Noetherian it would contradict the bullet, and if not it is off-scope.
events.doubts: Sidedness is disputed between sources (left PID in Wikipedia; right PID in a search summary). Whether the example is also Noetherian on the other side is not stated in any source I read, and the field's continued description of the bullet as open suggests it is not, but that is inference, not a source.
events.direction: Cuts against the one-sided form. Its bearing on the two-sided bullet depends on the unresolved fact in delivers.
events.object: A principal ideal domain, left or right (sources disagree), in which the powers of the Jacobson radical do not intersect to zero. Appears to be an explicit family of rings; construction not read.

events.what_happened: G. Cauchon, 'Sur l'intersection des puissances du radical d'un T-anneau noethérien', C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. A 279 (1974) 91–93 (MR 0347894). The title concerns intersections of powers of the radical in a Noetherian T-ring. Wikipedia cites it for the fully bounded Noetherian case. Not opened; the text was not available to me.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia's list of known cases, a positive result for fully bounded Noetherian rings, the same class as Jategaonkar 1974. The exact statement and whether it covers the whole class are unverified.
events.remains: Two-sided Noetherian rings outside the fully bounded class, as far as I can establish.
events.doubts: Only the title and Wikipedia's citation were seen; the content of the note is unverified.
events.direction: Positive for the fully bounded class per Wikipedia; consistent with the bullet's conclusion. Content not verified.

events.what_happened: A. V. Jategaonkar, 'Jacobson's conjecture and modules over fully bounded noetherian rings', J. Algebra 30 (1974) 103–121, proves the conjecture for fully bounded Noetherian rings. Key step as described by secondary sources: over such a ring, finitely generated essential extensions of simple left modules are Artinian, equivalently injective hulls of simple modules are locally Artinian. Ginn and Moss (Bull. AMS, 1975) extend the finiteness result to left and right Noetherian rings with projective finitely generated finitely embedded modules, per a search summary. The paper itself was not opened; the description rests on Wikipedia and secondary sources.
events.delivers: Proves that the intersection of the powers of J is zero for every fully bounded Noetherian ring (two-sided, per the secondary descriptions). Restriction: the fully bounded class.
events.remains: Every two-sided Noetherian ring that is not fully bounded, as far as my sources show.

checked_by.what_they_did: published the proof in 1974; cited as the source of the fully bounded case in Wikipedia

checked_by.qualification: authors of a 1975 Bull. AMS paper building on Jategaonkar's method; their qualifications were not checked
checked_by.what_they_did: extended the finiteness result to left and right Noetherian rings (per a search summary of their paper, which I did not open)

events.direction: Positive for the fully bounded class; consistent with the bullet's conclusion.

events.what_happened: I. N. Herstein and Lance Small, 'The intersection of the powers of the radical in Noetherian P.I. rings', Israel J. Math. 16 (1973) 176–180. Sources disagree on 1972 versus 1973 for the issue. The title indicates the PI case. Content not read; cited in Tuganbaev's 2010 reference list per a search summary.
events.delivers: Unverified. The title indicates a result on intersections of powers of the radical for Noetherian PI rings. If it proves the intersection is zero for all Noetherian PI rings, that is a positive class. I could not establish that, nor whether Noetherian PI rings already fall inside the fully bounded class.
events.remains: Unknown from my sources.
events.doubts: Content unknown. Whether the PI case is already covered by the fully bounded result is not established.
events.direction: Unknown from my sources; the title suggests a positive result for the PI class.

events.what_happened: T. H. Lenagan, 'Noetherian rings with Krull dimension one', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 15 (1977) 41–47 (citation from a reference list). Wikipedia cites it for the Krull-dimension-one case of the conjecture. A 1979 note by Hideo Sato describes Lenagan's structure result for two-sided Noetherian rings of Krull dimension one with artinian radical. Not opened.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia, establishes the conjecture for two-sided Noetherian rings of Krull dimension one. Restriction: Krull dimension one. Theorem statement not verified.
events.remains: Noetherian rings of Krull dimension two or more that are outside the other known classes, as far as known.
events.doubts: Theorem statement not verified. Sato's 1979 description is a structure statement, and I could not tie it directly to the intersection of powers.
events.direction: Positive for Krull dimension one, per Wikipedia.

events.what_happened: K. A. Brown and T. H. Lenagan, 'A note on Jacobson's conjecture for right Noetherian rings', Glasgow Math. J. 23 (1) (1982) 7–8 (DOI 10.1017/S0017089500004729). For a right Noetherian, right fully bounded ring R whose simple modules are all finitely generated over a central subring C, the powers of J(R) meet C in zero. Sources phrase the conclusion differently, and the formula did not load on the page I read. The note also contrasts Herstein's example with a similar ring that does satisfy the property. Cambridge page opened: abstract and theorem text not legible; the extract is consistent with this description. Some secondary citations date it 1980.
events.delivers: A one-sided positive result: right Noetherian, right fully bounded, simple modules finitely generated over a central C. The conclusion concerns the powers of J intersected with C. Does not give the two-sided statement.
events.remains: The two-sided statement for rings outside the right-fully-bounded, central-C class.

checked_by.who: K. A. Brown (Glasgow) and T. H. Lenagan (Edinburgh)
checked_by.what_they_did: wrote and published the note in the Glasgow Mathematical Journal

events.doubts: Year disputed: 1980 in some secondary citations, 1982 in the journal issue. The theorem text was not legible in my source, so the exact conclusion is unverified.
events.direction: Positive for the one-sided, right-fully-bounded class; consistent with the conjecture. Does not decide the two-sided case.

events.what_happened: A. V. Jategaonkar, 1982, cited by Wikipedia for Noetherian rings satisfying the second layer condition. The reference as mirrored in a search result is 'Solvable Lie algebras, polycyclic-by-finite groups and bimodule Krull dimension', Comm. Algebra 10 (1) (1982) 19–69, whose title does not mention the second layer condition. Jategaonkar's 1986 book 'Localization in Noetherian Rings' has a chapter on the second layer. Not opened.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia, the conjecture holds for Noetherian rings satisfying the second layer condition. Which paper establishes this is unresolved.
events.remains: Two-sided Noetherian rings without the second layer condition.
events.doubts: A citation mismatch, not a doubt about a result: the paper Wikipedia's reference points to, by title, concerns bimodule Krull dimension and solvable Lie algebras. The attribution of the second-layer result is unverified.
events.direction: Positive for second-layer rings, per Wikipedia; unverified.

events.what_happened: R. Krause, Arch. Math. 70 (6) (1998) 435–437 (DOI 10.1007/s000130050216). For a right Noetherian ring R of Krull dimension k with Jacobson radical J, using a new definition of ordinal powers J(α), shows J(ω·k+n) = 0 for some natural number n. Known from a search-result abstract; the Springer page redirected to a login page and the repository record was blocked.
events.delivers: Transfinite-power vanishing for right Noetherian rings of finite Krull dimension, under redefined ordinal powers. It is not stated for the finite intersection of powers that the bullet asks about. Whether it yields that intersection is zero is not established by my source.
events.remains: The bullet's statement for finite powers, and the two-sided case generally, as far as my source shows.
events.doubts: The result uses a redefined ordinal power J(α). Whether its ω-stage agrees with the classical intersection of the J^n is not established from the abstract. Restricted to right Noetherian rings of finite Krull dimension.
events.direction: A neighbouring transfinite statement. It does not directly assert that the intersection of the finite powers is zero, but it is consistent with the conjecture in spirit.

events.what_happened: A. A. Tuganbaev, 'A remark on the intersection of powers of the Jacobson radical', Fundam. Prikl. Mat. 15 (2) (2009) 207–209; English version J. Math. Sci. 167 (6) (2010) 868–869. Per a search-result abstract: for a left Noetherian, right distributive ring A, the intersection of the powers J(A)^k over k ≥ 1 is zero. The mathnet page refused the connection; the abstract is from a search summary.
events.revisions: Russian original 2009; English reprint in J. Math. Sci. 167 (2010)
events.delivers: Positive for left Noetherian rings that are also right distributive. The hypotheses are one-sided Noetherianity plus right distributivity, not two-sided Noetherianity.
events.remains: Two-sided Noetherian rings that are not right distributive, and rings Noetherian on one side only.
events.direction: Positive for a different hypothesis set (one-sided Noetherian plus right distributive), so a changed version of the problem.

events.what_happened: P. A. A. B. Carvalho, C. Lomp and D. Pusat-Yılmaz, 'Injective modules over down-up algebras', Glasgow Math. J. 52 (2010) 53–59 (arXiv:0906.2930; the June 2009 date is from the arXiv identifier). Per a search summary: for Noetherian down-up algebras A(α,β,γ), injective hulls of simple modules are locally Artinian when the roots of X²−αX−β are distinct roots of unity or both equal 1. Fully bounded ones are those module-finite over a central subalgebra. Not opened.
events.delivers: The stronger injective-hull property ◇ for a parameter family of down-up algebras. Secondary summaries say ◇ on a Noetherian ring implies the conjecture, so the conclusion follows for those algebras only. Restriction: the parameter family.
events.remains: Noetherian down-up algebras outside the parameter family, and the general two-sided case.
events.doubts: The implication from ◇ to the conjecture comes from secondary descriptions (Hatipoğlu's paper as summarised by search), not from the source I read.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; positive for a restricted family, via a stronger sufficient property.

events.what_happened: I. M. Musson, 'Finitely generated, non-artinian monolithic modules', arXiv:1104.1366 (submitted 7 April 2011). Surveys Noetherian rings with the injective-hull property ◇ (injective hulls of simple modules locally Artinian). Gives a general construction of algebras without ◇ and completes the classification of down-up algebras with ◇ in characteristic 0. Abstract read.
events.delivers: Shows ◇ fails for some Noetherian rings, so ◇ is not a route to the conjecture for all Noetherian rings. Does not decide the conjecture.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: Does not bear on the conjecture directly; shows a stronger sufficient property fails in general.

events.what_happened: Osman Can Hatipoğlu (listed as Can Hatipoğlu), 'Stable torsion theories and the injective hulls of simple modules', arXiv:1402.3157 (13 Feb 2014, single version). Torsion-theoretic characterization of left Noetherian rings whose simple left modules have locally Artinian injective hulls, with sufficient conditions in terms of torsion theories. Abstract read: it does not mention Jacobson's conjecture. Search summaries say the paper states that such rings satisfy the conjecture; that sentence is not in the abstract I read.
events.delivers: A reformulation of ◇ for left Noetherian rings. Per secondary summaries it gives the conjecture for such rings. It does not, in the abstract, prove the conjecture for any new class.
events.remains: The bullet, except for rings already known to have ◇.
events.doubts: The statement that ◇ implies the conjecture rests on secondary summaries; the abstract I read does not state it.
events.direction: Reformulates a sufficient condition; neither proves nor refutes the bullet.

events.what_happened: Nguyen Van Sanh, seminar talk at Institut Teknologi Bandung, 20 April 2012 (date from the seminar URL). Seminar abstract for a quasi-projective, finitely generated, fully bounded self-generator module M with S = End(M): if the Noetherian conditions on S and M hold, the intersection of the powers J^k(S) is zero. A seminar abstract only; no paper seen.
events.delivers: A module-theoretic analogue: the same vanishing for the endomorphism ring S of a fully bounded self-generator module under extra hypotheses. Not the bullet's ring-level statement.
events.remains: The bullet itself; this result is about S = End(M).
events.doubts: Seminar abstract only; no proof seen.
events.direction: An analogue for endomorphism rings of modules; discounted for the bullet.

events.what_happened: Bui Phuoc Minh and Nguyen Van Sanh, 'Some results related to Jacobson conjecture', East-West J. Math. 23 (1) (2021) 51–56 (doi 10.36853/ewjm0384). Per the abstract in a search result, they study the endomorphism rings of bounded and fully bounded modules and 'extended some results related to Jacobson's Conjecture'. Not opened.
events.delivers: Module-level extensions of the fully-bounded-type results, per the abstract. I did not see a ring-level result for the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was seen; the theorems are unverified.
events.direction: An analogue (module version); discounted for the bullet.

events.what_happened: Susumu Oda, 'Some Comments around The Examples against The Generalized Jacobian Conjecture', arXiv:0706.1138 (first submitted 8 June 2007; latest v99, 30 Nov 2022; v74 marked withdrawn). Concerns the Jacobian conjecture and a generalised form for Noetherian domains. It is not about Jacobson's conjecture. Recorded as a namesake only. Abstract read.
events.revisions: v1 8 Jun 2007; v99 30 Nov 2022; v74 withdrawn (per listing)
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet. It concerns the Jacobian conjecture (polynomial maps).
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: A different question (the Jacobian conjecture); discounted.

events.what_happened: Susumu Oda, 'On Open Embeddings of Affine Spaces in Affine Varieties and the Jacobian Conjecture', arXiv:1203.1691 (first submitted 8 March 2012; latest v39, 26 Sep 2026; v7–v13 withdrawn per the listing). Proves a result on open embeddings of affine space in normal affine surfaces, which the author says implies a generalised two-variable Jacobian statement. A page comment, as fetched, says the revision followed an AI-constructed counterexample to JC_n for n ≥ 3; the system is not named and the claim is unverified. A namesake only.
events.revisions: v1 8 Mar 2012; v7–v13 withdrawn; v39 26 Sep 2026
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet. It concerns the Jacobian conjecture (two-variable case and a generalised form).
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: A different question (the Jacobian conjecture); discounted.

events.what_happened: Jooyoung Shin, 'Jacobson radicals of Ore extensions', arXiv:2405.16342 (submitted 25 May 2024; a search summary gives a v2 in June 2024 and the listing I fetched gives a v3 on 9 Oct 2026). Describes J(R[x;σ,D]) for an automorphism σ and σ-derivation D, with a leading-coefficient description and nilness of J ∩ R under PI or locally nilpotent conditions. Partially answers a question of Greenfeld, Smoktunowicz and Ziembowski. Abstract and HTML full text read: no mention of Jacobson's conjecture, no Noetherian hypothesis, no intersection of powers of J, and no AI system (the acknowledgement thanks Professor Mikhail Chebotar).
events.revisions: v1 25 May 2024; v2 June 2024 (per search summary); v3 9 Oct 2026 (per listing as fetched)
events.delivers: Results on the Jacobson radical of Ore extensions, not on powers of J in a Noetherian ring. Restrictions: PI or locally nilpotent derivation conditions; no Noetherian assumption.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: Off-scope: about Jacobson radicals of skew extensions, not the intersection of powers of J in a Noetherian ring.

events.what_happened: J. Cimprič and M. Schötz, 'Left Jacobson Rings', arXiv:2503.16005 (submitted 20 Mar 2025; v3 9 Mar 2026). Defines strongly and weakly left Jacobson rings (every semiprime or prime left ideal is an intersection of maximal left ideals), with a one-sided noncommutative Nullstellensatz for A[x1,...,xn] where A is finite-dimensional. Abstract and HTML full text read: no mention of Jacobson's conjecture or of powers of the Jacobson radical, and no AI system.
events.revisions: v1 20 Mar 2025; v2 June 2025 (per search summary); v3 9 Mar 2026
events.delivers: Results on maximal left ideals and Nullstellensätze for rings of polynomials over finite-dimensional algebras. No bearing on the intersection of powers of J.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: Off-scope: a different property (Jacobson-type ideal intersections), not the vanishing of the intersection of powers of J.

events.what_happened: Press and aggregator snippets (no primary source opened) report that on 20 July 2026 Levent Alpöge, listed as Harvard and Anthropic, announced a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture (polynomial maps with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant) that a model named in the snippets as 'Claude Fable 5' produced, and that independent checks followed. This is the Jacobian conjecture, not Jacobson's conjecture. Recorded as a namesake that a name-matching pass could confuse with this bullet.
events.delivers: Nothing on this bullet.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.doubts: Unverified: only news and aggregator snippets were seen. The claim concerns a different problem.
events.direction: A different question (the Jacobian conjecture); discounted for this bullet.

disputes.summary: Sidedness of Jategaonkar's counterexample: Wikipedia says left principal ideal domain; a search summary says right principal ideal domains whose right ideals are the powers of J. Relevant because a one-sided counterexample bears on the two-sided bullet only if it is also two-sided Noetherian.
Year of Brown and Lenagan's note: 1982 in the Glasgow Mathematical Journal issue; 1980 in some secondary citations.

Wikipedia attributes the second-layer case to Jategaonkar 1982, but the reference title given in a mirror (bimodule Krull dimension and solvable Lie algebras) does not mention the second layer condition.
Herstein and Small's paper is dated 1972 in some reference lists and 1973 in others (volume 16, pages 176–180 of Israel J. Math. in both).

summary: I ran 40 web searches and opened 15 sources: the Wikipedia article (fetched copy reports last edit 3 November 2023), arXiv abstracts for 1402.3157, 1104.1366, 1711.10580, 2405.16342 and 2503.16005 (with HTML full texts for the last two), 2608.09370, 2604.03789, 2204.10307, 1203.1691 and 0706.1138, the Brown–Lenagan Cambridge page (abstract and theorem text not legible), and Epoch's FrontierMath page. Seven primary pages refused the fetch or redirected (Springer ×2, PNAS, Bielefeld, mathnet, the UIS skew-PBW article, and themoonlight), so the pre-2024 results rest on the Wikipedia article, search-result abstracts and secondary citations, and are marked opened: false. Nothing in the window moves a quantity the bullet names. The in-window items I could read are off-scope: Shin's Ore-extension preprint (May 2024) and Cimprič–Schötz's left-Jacobson-rings preprint (March 2025). Neither mentions the conjecture or powers of J, and neither names an AI system. Every source describes the conjecture as open in general. The positive classes all predate the window: commutative Noetherian rings (Krull), fully bounded Noetherian rings (Jategaonkar 1974; Cauchon 1974), Krull dimension one (Lenagan 1977), the second layer condition (Jategaonkar 1982, attribution unclear), right fully bounded rings with central simple-module data (Brown–Lenagan), and left Noetherian plus right distributive rings (Tuganbaev 2009). The known counterexamples are to the one-sided question (Herstein 1965; Jategaonkar 1968). Close calls: (a) Shin 2024 and Cimprič–Schötz 2025 concern Jacobson radicals and Jacobson-type ideal intersections, not powers of J, so I treated them as off-scope; a reader could call them neighbours. (b) The injective-hull property ◇ (Carvalho–Lomp–Pusat-Yılmaz 2010; Musson 2011; Hatipoğlu 2014) is a stronger sufficient condition. Sources say it implies the conjecture, but that implication comes from secondary summaries, not the abstracts I read, so I recorded these as restricted-class or discounted events. (c) Krause 1998 uses redefined transfinite powers; whether it bears on the intersection of the finite powers is unclear. AI involvement: no source names an AI system in connection with this bullet's problem. The AI-involved claims I found concern the Jacobian conjecture (namesake, recorded as alpoge-2026-jacobian-namesake from snippets only) and an unrelated commutative-algebra problem (arXiv 2604.03789, not recorded). This absence rests on web search and on the trackers I could reach; the Vibe Mathed site and the Erdős wiki were not reachable or not opened, so it is not a complete check.
competing_reading: A reader who counts Shin 2024 or Cimprič–Schötz 2025 as in-window progress would say the window is not empty; I read both as neighbours that move no quantity the bullet names. A reader who treats the Jacobian-conjecture AI claim as an AI event for this bullet would be wrong by name alone; I recorded it so a later pass can see why it was set aside. A reader who takes Herstein–Small 1973 or Krause 1998 as settling a broad class would need their full statements, which I could not read.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Whether Jategaonkar's 1968 counterexample is also right Noetherian: if it is two-sided Noetherian it refutes the bullet; if not it is off-scope. (2) The statement of Herstein–Small 1973: whether it proves the intersection is zero for all Noetherian PI rings, and whether those rings already lie in the fully bounded class. (3) Readable theorem statements for Cauchon 1974, Lenagan 1977, Jategaonkar 1982 and Brown–Lenagan 1982, to fix the known classes exactly. (4) Dated arXiv (math.RA, math.AC) and zbMATH/MathSciNet searches for 'Jacobson conjecture' and 'powers of the Jacobson radical' from 26 January 2024 to 12 October 2026, plus citing searches for Jategaonkar 1974. I could not run these. (5) The Ginn–Moss 1975 paper, to see whether it claims more than the finiteness result.
